note: Language-agnostic conformance vectors for check() over a NON-ARCHE program (graph reachability + byte-ordering), so genericity is demonstrated, not asserted. Every {rs,go} binding replays this file and must agree on every outcome. Pins ONLY the FIRM structural rejection band (branch on the code string, never on detail). The host-extension band (builtin_failed/leaf_rejected/rule_inadmissible + consumer sub-codes) is deliberately NOT here: it is pinned in each consumer's own suite (see the rs runner's host_band unit tests). Two structural codes are decoder-only and unreachable from well-typed input, so they have no case here: non_ground_conclusion (a GroundLiteral's args are ontos Values, always ground) and unknown_node_kind (Node is a closed 3-variant enum). This is grammar/shape conformance; account-codec BYTE vectors are deferred until quote/reify byte form + VarId alpha-normalization settle (contract §9). Authoring notation: term = {atom:<hex>} | {atom_str:<utf8 sugar>} | {tuple:[...]} | {var:<id>} | {nest:{functor:<utf8>, times:N, leaf:<term>}} (#2731: functor(functor(...leaf...)), `times` Tuple[Atom(functor), ·] levels around `leaf`, expanded by a loop, so a term past any JSON parser's nesting limit is authored flat); pred = a utf8 string; ground_literal = {pred, args:[ground term...]}; node = {kind:rule|builtin|leaf, conclusion, ...}. The demo_v1 profile (implemented identically per language): Theory owns 'lt' and Holds iff lt(a,b) with a<b bytewise; LeafVerifier extensional={edge}, admits any edge leaf; RuleAdmissibility = always-admit; Context = unit. Rows that state a `report` pin check()'s work counters tri-core (#4206): counters_version and all 17 counters, hand-computed from the counting rules in contract/rs/src/check/report.rs, never pasted from an implementation. PINNED vs COUNTED (#4206, the coordinator's rule: never pin by hand a value the checker's own order of work decides). A report value is either an integer, pinned exactly, or the string "counted", which asserts the counter is counted (a non-negative integer) without pinning its value. Pinned wherever report.rs's rules fix the value from the row's derivation, program and profile: the walk's counters (nodes_walked and the three kinds, premises_pos/neg, theory_decisions, leaf_verifications, admissibility_checks, max_depth_reached, max_term_depth_reached) and certs_verified; and, on a row whose certificate is verified to completion, the certificate meters (cert_tables_read, cert_rows_read, join_steps_used, groundings_enumerated), which are then totals over the certificate's own tables and closure. A row whose certificate is refused partway (cert_canonical_rows_unsorted) states those four as "counted": how much was read before the refusal depends on the order the checker visits tables. check() Outcome equality compares the verdict only (checker SPI v2), so this report pin is the only place the counters are compared. No vector row exercises certs_memo_hits (a memo hit needs a second check of one world), and no check.json row cites a certificate, so negation.json's report rows carry the certificate counters.

cases.name: leaf_with_hex_atom_and_tuple_arg_accept
cases.note: Exercises the {atom:<hex>} form (0xff — a byte atom_str cannot express) and the {tuple:[...]} recursion, so a second-language parser's hex-decode and tuple paths are pinned by the shared oracle, not just rs-local. edge is extensional, so the leaf is admitted regardless of its (structured) arguments.

cases.name: root_at_index_max_out_of_range
cases.note: #2682 ruling A: the root at INDEX_MAX = 2^53 - 1, the largest index the contract's decoder admits (vectors/derivation_wire.json root_at_index_max_decodes). It passes decode in every core, so check refuses it by its FIRM root_out_of_range, the same as root 5 above.

cases.name: root_past_32_bit_offset_out_of_range
cases.note: #2735: the root at 2^32 + 5, past a 32-bit offset and inside the contract's domain (vectors/derivation_wire.json root_past_32_bit_offset_decodes). An index is an INTEGER, not a host offset: it passes decode in every core on every build, and check refuses it by its FIRM root_out_of_range, the same as root 5 above.

cases.name: term_too_deep_tuple_arg
cases.note: issue #253 — a single-term NESTING-depth cap in the trusted path. edge(pair(a,b), 0xff) carries a tuple argument of structural depth 2; with max_term_depth=1 it exceeds the bound and is REJECTED term_too_deep (a new FIRM structural code), tri-core. This pins the bound MECHANISM via a tight limit on a shallow term (a literally tens-of-thousands-deep JSON term would stress each CLI's recursive vector decoder); the no-stack-overflow property at the real crashing depth is proven in each core's adversarial unit tests. The depth measurement is itself iterative (Term::depth_le / value_depth_le), so checking an over-deep term does not overflow. Distinct from too_deep (DAG/premise-chain depth).

cases.name: term_within_depth_bound_accept
cases.note: issue #253 — the SAME edge(pair(a,b), 0xff) term (depth 2) is ACCEPTED under max_term_depth=2: the bound only refuses a term that EXCEEDS it, never weakening the accept path. Pins that a within-bound term still passes, tri-core.

cases.name: term_depth_alone_keeps_the_other_budgets_accept
cases.note: issue #253 — the SAME edge(pair(a,b), 0xff) term (depth 2) is ACCEPTED under max_term_depth=2: the bound only refuses a term that EXCEEDS it, never weakening the accept path. Pins that a within-bound term still passes, tri-core.

cases.name: witness_lane_at_least_3_distinct_accept
cases.note: ADR-0023 / #589 monotone witness lane: '≥k distinct' is certifiable TODAY by positive witnesses + owned builtin nodes, NO certificate and NO new account node. at_least_3_distinct(a,b,c) over edge(a,b),edge(b,c) is pruned by the strict-order chain lt(a,b),lt(b,c),lt(a,c) — three owned `lt` Builtin nodes that witness a,b,c are pairwise distinct (a strict total order is irreflexive). demo_v1 owns `lt`, not `\==`, so the tri-core ACCEPT vector uses lt as the owned disequality witness; the matching `\==` TermTheory accept AND the bogus-witness REJECT (a repeated value fails an owned builtin, so check() refuses — host-extension band, language-local per this file's note) are pinned end-to-end in conformance/rs/tests/witness_lane_distinct.rs.

cases.name: term_depth_256_at_the_default_accept
cases.note: #2731 (seat:caa's ruling): the DEFAULT policy, with no limits override. edge(s(s(...s(z)...)), b) carries a first argument exactly 256 term levels deep (255 s-levels around the atom z, the atom counting as one level), which is check's default max_term_depth in every core, so it is ACCEPTED tri-core. derivation_wire.json's ground_arg_256_term_levels_decodes is the same conclusion on the wire, and it decodes in every core: rs's decoder refused it until #2731, which made the spec's tri-core promise false at the defaults.

cases.name: term_depth_257_past_the_default_term_too_deep
cases.note: #2731: the same at 257 term levels, one past the default max_term_depth, so check REFUSES it term_too_deep in every core. The decoder accepts the same conclusion (derivation_wire.json's ground_arg_257_term_levels_decodes): the depth refusal belongs to check alone.
